chunk_findings.detail: Previous confirmed #2 still holds. Adding `>` to `_COMMENT_BOUNDARY` does not change top-level parsing because `_scan` is untouched; `echo ok >#x; git push origin main` is still refused, even though in bash the `#` after `>` starts a comment to the end of the line and `git push` never runs.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/forbidden.py:_scan

chunk_findings.detail: `for _ in range(16)` still caps how deeply the guard descends through nested `sh -c` layers. Construct a command by wrapping `git push origin main` in 17 shell-quoted `sh -c` layers, e.g. repeatedly building `"sh -c " + shlex.quote(inner)`. At runtime the innermost `git push origin main` is executed, but `_commands` stops after 16 levels, so that forbidden command never reaches `cmds` and `F.check` returns no refusal. The comment says “still capped”; a fixed cap is a bypass for any depth beyond it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/forbidden.py:_commands
